name: One-pot cottage-cheese TUNA pasta (spelt) — protein-packed

source.author: Instagram — raz_yahav (Hebrew caption)
source.notes: One-pot creamy high-protein pasta. Original uses regular pasta — swapped to SPELT (user's usual). This is the TUNA version; a canned-salmon version (onepot_cottage_salmon_spelt_pasta) removes the mercury flag and adds omega-3/vitamin D. Cottage 5%, yellow cheese 9%; values from references. Big batch; servings assumed 6.

ingredients.note: use LIGHT/skipjack — see her safety note
TASTE FIRST — cottage/cheese/tuna are already very salty; likely needs much less

steps: Simmer spelt pasta + tuna + aromatics in the water in one wide pot until pasta is al dente and water absorbed; stir in cottage + yellow cheese off high heat until creamy.

batch_totals.note: Sodium ~9,000 mg batch (~1,500 mg/serving) — mostly the 1.5 tsp added salt on top of salty cottage/cheese/tuna. Cutting the added salt is the biggest lever.

him.verdict: A seriously protein-packed comfort pasta — ~52 g protein for ~582 kcal (~9 g protein per 100 kcal) from cottage + tuna + yellow cheese, with spelt's whole-grain fiber (~6 g/serving) and big calcium. The spelt swap already improved it (more protein/fiber, fewer refined carbs). The one thing dragging it down hard is SODIUM: ~1,500 mg/serving (≈65% of a day's limit) from 1.5 tsp added salt stacked on already-salty cottage, cheese and canned tuna.
suggested_mods: Skip or halve the added salt — the cottage/cheese/tuna already bring plenty; taste first. Biggest lever by far
Stir in spinach or peas at the end for folate/fiber and to lighten the carb share
The salmon version adds omega-3 + vitamin D (sperm micros) — see onepot_cottage_salmon_spelt_pasta

her_preconception.verdict: Nutrient-rich for her — high protein + calcium (cottage + cheese) + selenium — but it carries the tuna mercury flag AND very high sodium, so it's a 'fine occasionally, mind the details' rather than a staple. Per-serving tuna is ~½ can, which helps.
prenatal_highlights: selenium from tuna; whole-grain spelt fiber

safety_advisories.note: TUNA = mercury. Use LIGHT/skipjack canned tuna (not albacore); once actively trying/pregnant keep total tuna to ~2 servings/week. The canned-salmon version removes this flag entirely and adds omega-3 + vitamin D.
Very high sodium (~1,500 mg/serving) — ease it in pregnancy.

suggested_mods: Prefer the salmon version for the preconception lens
Cut the added salt; add spinach for folate

cooking_guide: For more depth, soften the sliced red onion + garlic in a little oil in the wide pot first (optional but worth it).
Add the dry spelt pasta, drained tuna, pepper, chili and 2–2.5 cups water to the pot; bring to a simmer.

Cook uncovered, stirring often so the pasta doesn't stick, until the pasta is al dente and most of the water is absorbed (~10–12 min). Spelt can go from firm to soft quickly, so check early; add a splash more water if it dries before the pasta is done.
Lower the heat, then stir in the cottage cheese and grated yellow cheese until melted and creamy — keep it gentle (hard-boiling cottage can turn it grainy).
TASTE before adding the 1.5 tsp salt — the cottage, cheese and tuna are already very salty, so you'll likely need much less or none. This is the single biggest lever on the dish.
Rest 2–3 min off the heat to thicken; finish with fresh herbs and chili.
Tip: stir a couple of handfuls of spinach or some peas in at the end for folate + fiber.
